approach: Write one new design note, docs/design/continuous-landing.md, making landing a continuous drain step. At verifier pass the job joins the one ordered landing queue (async-drain.md sections 6 and 7). The queue head rebases, then merges its pull request with the existing REST path (`land_pr`, `merge_via_rest = true`). A job whose poll ends pending (`Landing::Waiting`) stays in the queue and is polled again inside the drain, for a bounded time at the head; it then steps aside and keeps its order, or goes back to the user. The self-rebuild keeps its invariant: landings wait while it builds, because a landing moves the checkout the build reads (drain.rs:2399-2401, lock at 2403). The note changes only when the rebuild runs. It is coalesced, via the existing `rebuild_due` flag (drain.rs:1726, 2404), into one run at a batch boundary where no job is in a landing or records stage, with a bound on how many landings or how long it may be deferred. A separate-worktree build is a rejected-for-now option, with its costs stated. The note labels 420.0 min as the review's prediction, names the measurement (median over the newest 20 landings, verifier end to landing record, against 464.5), and asks the next review to report rebuild time separately. Small additive edits go in async-drain.md (pointers), docs/decisions.md (D155) and CHANGELOG.md. No code or governance file changes.

decisions.choice: Reuse the existing REST merge in `land_pr` (the `merge_via_rest` path), run by the queue head, as the 'automatic merge'. Do not depend on a host auto-merge setting.
decisions.reason: The merge call, the wait for checks, the landing intent and landing records and the merged-content check exist and are tested (crates/athena-core/src/gh/landing.rs:228-300; native-pr-landing.md section 5). Host squash-only and linear-history rules (docs/system-facts.md) are handled there. The new work is when the merge starts and who waits for it, not how it merges.

rejected.option: Enable the host's native auto-merge on the pull request at enqueue
rejected.why: It needs a repository setting the code does not show to be on (an open Host question). The merge would happen outside the ordered queue, so order and the landing-intent write (records-history.md) would no longer hold.

rejected.option: Add a new merge code path for the drain
rejected.why: It duplicates `land_pr` and its safety checks for no saving.

decisions.choice: Release the worker at verifier pass. The queue head rebases, waits for CI and merges. A job whose poll ends pending (`Landing::Waiting`) stays in the ordered queue and is polled again inside the drain (the parked CI wait of async-drain.md sections 6 and 7), instead of being passed over for a later `athena land --pr`. Its time at the head is bounded: after a limit H the job steps aside and keeps its order (it is polled again behind the job that landed, and re-enters at the head once its checks are green), and after a second limit it goes back to the user with its pull request open. H starts at one further poll window (the 30 x 20 s = 10 min of wiring.rs:42-48) and is set from the phase measurement of build job 1; the note gives it as a parameter, not a measured value. A merge the host refuses under its repository rules is mapped to Waiting today (drain.rs:3131-3135, 3142-3149), so a build job must tell it apart from pending checks (the report's `checks` field) and send it to the user at once, not wait H.
decisions.reason: Today `Drain::land` holds the `landing` lock for the whole poll, up to 10 min (drain.rs:1715; wiring.rs:42-48). A pending poll gives `Landing::Waiting` (drain.rs:3142-3149), the job is marked 'waiting to merge', `work` returns `ItemEnd::Waiting` (drain.rs:1860) and the item is passed over (drain.rs:2511). A later, separate `athena land --pr` finishes it (drain.rs:128-130). That tail is the likeliest home of a 440-minute median, since the median CI run is 583 s (warm-baseline-build.md 2.1). Strict first-in first-out with no limit would let one job whose merge the host keeps refusing block every later landing and cancel the saving, so the limit is part of the design (finding 2).

rejected.why: async-drain.md section 9 alternative a: jobs would land racing, with no order and no conflict return.
It does not address the queue, the passed-over Waiting jobs or the lock wait, in a stage more than 20 times the median CI run.

rejected.option: Strict first-in first-out at the head with no time limit
rejected.why: A Waiting job that never clears (a refused merge, a CI run that never finishes) blocks all later landings (head-of-line blocking).

decisions.choice: Keep the rebuild invariant stated at drain.rs:2399-2401: landings wait while the build runs, because a landing moves the checkout the build reads (`rebuild_if_due` takes `self.landing`, drain.rs:2403). The note chooses option two of the review finding: keep the lock, but run the rebuild once per batch, at a batch boundary, instead of after each landing that touched BUILD_PATHS. Today `finish` calls `rebuild_if_due` after every `ItemEnd::Landed` (drain.rs:2431), and the `rebuild_due` flag already merges several landings into one build (`|=` at drain.rs:1726, `take` at 2404), but with one landing at a time each flag is usually taken before the next landing. The change: the call waits until no verified job is queued and no job is in a landing or records stage (the async-drain.md section 7 rule, D140), or until a bound is reached (at most K landings or M minutes since the first due flag, whichever is first; K and M are parameters set after build job 5 measures rebuild time), so a busy queue cannot starve the rebuild and the installed binary does not go stale without limit. Cost, stated in the note: lock time saved = (rebuilds today - rebuilds after batching) x R, where R is the duration of one `setup.sh` run; R is not recorded (hestia.md:277), so the note gives the formula and makes R the output of build job 5, not a number. The cost of the choice is a longer time on the old binary, and landings that run on it. A failed rebuild keeps D140: landing is held, no new producers start, and nothing lands on a main the drain cannot build.
decisions.reason: It keeps the invariant with no change to `setup.sh` or to what the build reads. It reuses the existing flag and lock. The saving is only in the lock time that other jobs' spans carry, and the note says so plainly: a job's own rebuild already runs after its own landing record (drain.rs:2428-2431; status.rs:805-813), so the note does not call it a measurement effect for that job's span. The first reading's claim that the rebuild 'no longer holds the landing lock' is withdrawn.

rejected.option: Option one: build from a fixed commit in a separate worktree so landings carry on while it builds
rejected.why: It would remove the lock but needs a second cold `target/` (the disk budget of async-drain.md section 5, and the cold-build time of warm-baseline-build.md), and the real rebuild runs `setup.sh` in the checkout (drain.rs:137, 3274-3278), so it would change what installs and from where. It is recorded in the note as a later option, taken only if build job 5 shows the batched lock time is still large.

rejected.option: Drop the lock and run the rebuild beside landings
rejected.why: A landing would move the checkout under the build; this is the invariant at drain.rs:2399-2401.

rejected.option: Say part of the 420.0 min is a measurement change because the rebuild leaves the span
rejected.why: The code shows a job's own rebuild already falls after its landing record.

rejected.option: Count the whole saving as latency removed
rejected.why: hestia.md:277 says no record separates the rebuild, so how much of the 440.1 min it is would be unmeasured.

decisions.choice: Make the first build job a measurement of the 440.1 min by phase: wait for the drain, queue wait, lock wait, CI poll, time in Waiting before a later `athena land --pr`, merge, and rebuild. Raise limits only afterwards.
decisions.reason: The snapshot has no records or THROUGHPUT.md, and the code cannot say which phase dominates. The 420.0 min is the review's prediction; the note labels it that and builds the evidence step first. The limits H, K and M are set from it.

rejected.why: A design that cannot show where 440.1 min goes risks fixing the wrong wait.

decisions.choice: Edit async-drain.md only by adding short pointers and renumbering nothing. Add one decision D155 in the existing format. D155 and the note refer to D140 and to async-drain.md without the words 'amends', 'supersedes' or 'superseded by' next to a decision id. Add one CHANGELOG Unreleased entry.

risks.risk: Ordering: releasing the worker at verifier pass lets later jobs enqueue while an earlier one waits on CI, and they could land out of order.
risks.mitigation: The note keeps one landing at a time under the existing ordered queue (async-drain.md section 6) and first-in first-out by verifier pass. The merged-content check in `land_pr` stays as the safety net. The only departure from strict order is a Waiting job stepping aside after the limit H, which the note states, with its place kept.

risks.risk: Head-of-line blocking: a Waiting job at the head can stall every later landing. `landing_from_report` (drain.rs:3131-3135, 3142-3149) maps a merge the host refused under its repository rules to Waiting, and that state may never clear. With strict first-in first-out one such job blocks the queue and the saving disappears.
risks.mitigation: Bound the time at the head to H (initially one more poll window of 10 min, wiring.rs:42-48; set after build job 1). On reaching H the job steps aside, keeps its order and is polled again; after a second limit it goes back to the user with its pull request open. A refused merge is told apart from pending checks and sent to the user at once. The note lists this as its own risk and as a test for the build job.

risks.risk: Rebuild lock invariant and failure: the rebuild reads the checkout, and a landing moves it (drain.rs:2399-2401). Running the rebuild beside landings would build a moving tree; deferring it too long leaves a stale binary, and a failed rebuild could let jobs land on a main Athena cannot build.
risks.mitigation: The note keeps the lock, so no landing overlaps a build. It batches the rebuild to a boundary with no job in a landing or records stage, with the bound K landings or M minutes so a busy queue cannot starve it. The section 7 rule (D140) holds: a failed rebuild holds landing, starts no new producers and stops the drain with the build output. The note gives the saving as a formula, (rebuilds avoided) x R, with R unmeasured, and keeps the separate-worktree build (second cold `target/`, disk budget, setup.sh change) as a later option.

risks.risk: Merge conflicts: a job waiting in the queue meets a moved main.
risks.mitigation: The note reuses the section 6 rebase, the held-back conflict case, `max_conflict_returns` and the re-check rule (`rebase_needs_recheck`; `recheck_after_rebase` at drain.rs:1716). It says the real conflict hold wiring is a dependency of the build jobs.

risks.risk: The saving is misread. A job's own rebuild already falls after its landing record (drain.rs:2428-2431), so it is not in that job's span; the rebuild shows up only as lock contention in later jobs' spans.
risks.mitigation: The note labels 420.0 min as the review's prediction and derives the implied remainder (464.5 - 420.0 = 44.5 min, an estimate). It explains the rebuild as lock contention, asks the next review to report rebuild time separately, and compares the 20 newest landings after the change.

risks.risk: The 440.1 minutes may be mostly the wait before the drain reaches the job, or time in Waiting before a later `athena land --pr`, so the design would remove less than predicted.
risks.mitigation: The note makes the phase split (including Waiting as its own phase) the first build job and states that the saving depends on it.

risks.mitigation: Verify the new and edited files hold no banned word, no email-like text and no 'amends', 'supersedes' or 'superseded by' next to a decision id; `cargo test --locked` would catch each.

demonstrations.fails_without: A banned word or email-like text fails the policy scan. 'amends', 'supersedes' or 'superseded by' with a decision id in D155 adds a hit and fails backtest.rs:131. A malformed '## D155 · ...' header or missing field fails the decisions readers. A removed CHANGELOG phrase fails the include_str! `contains` assertions.
